1.title: Providers: Installing, Versioning and Using Several
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Providers: Installing, Versioning and Using Several. It covers the exam area two. Terraform fundamentals. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. two A Install and version Terraform providers. two B Describe how Terraform uses providers. two C Write Terraform configuration using multiple providers. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Terraform fundamentals. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What a provider is
1.text: What a provider is. A provider is a plugin that lets Terraform talk to an A P I (a cloud, a sass service, a platform). Terraform core reads the configuration and builds the plan; providers create, read, update and delete the real resources.

1.title: What a provider is, continued
1.text: What a provider is. The figure shows this: Terraform core calls provider plugins, which call the platform A P Is.

1.title: What a provider is, continued
1.text: What a provider is. Where providers come from. The Terraform Registry ( registry dot terraform dot io ) by default. Tiers. Official (Hashi Corp), partner (a technology company), community. Source address. namespace slash type, for example hashicorp slash aws. Downloaded by. terraform init. What a provider defines. Resource types and data sources, such as aws instance. Exam tip: Terraform core does not know any cloud; providers do. terraform init downloads the providers.

1.title: Installing and versioning providers
1.text: Installing and versioning providers. You declare the providers a configuration needs in a terraform block with required providers, and configure them in provider blocks. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Installing and versioning providers, continued
1.text: Installing and versioning providers. required version. The Terraform C L I versions allowed. required providers. Which providers, where from ( source ) and which versions ( version ). provider block. Configuration of one provider: region, credentials, endpoints. Version constraints. or no operator. Exactly that version. ! Anything except that version. Comparisons. about. Pessimistic constraint: allow only the rightmost version part to increase; about five dot zero means at least five point zero and below six point zero; about five dot one dot zero means at least five point one.zero and below five point two. Exam tip: about five dot zero allows five point one, five point two and so on, but not six point zero. Pin versions so that a new provider release does not change your infrastructure unexpectedly.

1.title: The dependency lock file
1.text: The dependency lock file. terraform init writes dot terraform dot lock dot hcl, which records the exact provider versions and checksums that were selected. Purpose. Same provider versions for every run and every team member. Commit it? Yes, commit it to version control. Update it. terraform init -upgrade selects newer versions that match the constraints. Do not edit by hand. Terraform maintains it.

1.title: Using several providers
1.text: Using several providers. Different providers. List each in required providers and configure each (for example aws and random ). Same provider, several configurations. Add alias to extra provider blocks (for example two regions) and choose with the provider meta-argument.

1.title: Using several providers, continued
1.text: Using several providers. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Using several providers, continued
1.text: Using several providers. A resource without a provider argument uses the default (unaliased) configuration of its provider. Exam tip: Aliases are for several configurations of the same provider, such as two regions. Use provider aws dot west on the resource.

1.title: How Terraform uses providers at run time
1.text: How Terraform uses providers at run time. init. Terraform installs providers and records versions in the lock file. plan. The provider reads current infrastructure and Terraform compares it with the configuration. apply. The provider makes the A P I calls to create, update or destroy. terraform providers lists the providers a configuration uses.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which command downloads the providers that a configuration needs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: terraform init. terraform init installs the required providers and modules and creates the lock file.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A configuration states version equals "about greater than five point zero" for a provider. Which versions are allowed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Any version from five point zero up to but not including six point zero. The pessimistic operator allows increases of the rightmost part only, so five point zero up to below six point zero.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What does the dependency lock file record? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The selected provider versions and their checksums. The lock file records which provider versions and checksums were selected, so everyone uses the same ones.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team needs to create resources in two regions with the same provider. What should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Two provider blocks, one with an alias. An extra provider block with an alias gives a second configuration, selected by the provider argument.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which command updates the selected provider versions within the allowed constraints? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: terraform init -upgrade. terraform init -upgrade chooses the newest versions that match the constraints and updates the lock file.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Where does Terraform download providers from by default? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The Terraform Registry. Providers are downloaded from the Terraform Registry unless another source is configured.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a provider do? Answer: Lets Terraform talk to an A P I and manage its resources. Question two. What block lists the required providers? Answer: required providers inside the terraform block. Question three. What file records provider versions? Answer: .terraform.lock.hcl.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does about greater than five point zero mean? Answer: At least five point zero and below six point zero. Question five. What is a provider alias for? Answer: Several configurations of the same provider. Question six. Should the lock file be committed? Answer: Yes.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Providers: plugins from the Registry; installed by init; define resource types. Declare: required providers with source and version; provider block configures. Constraints: equals,! equals, comparisons, about greater than (rightmost part only). Lock file:.terraform.lock.hcl; commit; init -upgrade to move forward. Several: different providers listed; same provider with alias and provider equals.
